recipes.title: Usable observations per month
recipes.question: How much usable Sentinel-2 data does each month have over the catchment?
formula: clear(p, d) = 1 if the scene classification of pixel p on date d is 4 (vegetation) or 5 (not vegetated) and red and near-infrared are present, else 0
dates(p, t) = number of distinct dates d in month t with clear(p, d) = 1
accepted(p, t) = 1 if dates(p, t) >= 3, else 0
valid_fraction(t) = sum over catchment pixels of accepted(p, t) / number of catchment pixels
status(t) = available if valid_fraction(t) >= 0.70; insufficient if below; missing if no clear date

parameters.name: stratum
allowed: catchment
parameters.default: catchment

applicability.check: validated NDVI bundle for the case geometry revision

assumptions: The Sen2Cor scene classification separates clear land from cloud, shadow and snow well enough to count usable dates
failureModes: Snow and bright cloud confused; terrain shadow lost preferentially on north-facing slopes; snow edges kept as clear
standardLimitations: Reduced QA (scene classification only): snow, snow edges and terrain shadow can survive the mask.
Coverage counts how much data passed the mask; it says nothing about vegetation condition.
In winter months the accepted pixels favour the valley floor and south-facing slopes, because snow and shade remove the others; the area value then describes those pixels, not the whole catchment.
This version summarizes the catchment only; per-stratum coverage is not computed yet.
recipes.registration: Catalog row before data; formula and parameters written with the first run (2026-10-27)
recipes.formulaPlain: A pixel-month counts when it has at least 3 clear dates. A month is available when such pixels cover at least 70% of the catchment.

recipes.title: Departure from the same month in 2019 to 2025
recipes.question: Was this month's NDVI unusual for this place and calendar month, compared with 2019 to 2025?
formula: NDVI = (NIR - Red) / (NIR + Red), surface reflectance = DN / 10000, per clear observation
N(p, y, m) = median of NDVI over the clear dates of pixel p in month m of year y, used only where accepted(p, t) = 1
ref(p, m) = median of N(p, y, m) over the years 2019 to 2025 in which it exists; defined only with at least 4 such years
ref_loyo(p, y, m) = the same median over the years other than y; defined only with at least 4 such years
dep(p, y, m) = N(p, y, m) - ref(p, m); dep_loyo(p, y, m) = N(p, y, m) - ref_loyo(p, y, m)
common-valid pixels: dep(p, y, m) defined; the month's summary is withheld if they cover less than 70% of the catchment
summary = area median of dep over common-valid pixels, with spatial IQR (25th to 75th percentile); the same for dep_loyo

parameters.name: reference
allowed: all_years
leave_one_year_out
parameters.default: all_years

parameters.name: stratum
allowed: catchment
parameters.default: catchment

sensitivitySet: all_years and leave_one_year_out references, both always computed and shown together

applicability.check: at least 4 accepted years for the calendar month over 70% of the catchment

assumptions: A per-pixel median of 7 years describes what is usual for that pixel and month
failureModes: Dry years inside the reference pull it down; snow-affected months; processing baseline mix (about 0.002 to 0.003 reflectance)
standardLimitations: The reference is a short period (2019 to 2025), not a climate normal.
A departure describes how this month differs from other years here; it does not say why.
The spatial IQR is variability across pixels, not a confidence interval.
In winter months the accepted pixels favour the valley floor and south-facing slopes, because snow and shade remove the others; the area value then describes those pixels, not the whole catchment.
recipes.registration: Catalog row before data; formula and parameters written with the first run (2026-10-27)
recipes.formulaPlain: Each pixel's monthly NDVI is compared with its median for the same month over 2019 to 2025, and over the other years only. The departures are summarized by their area median and spatial spread.

recipes.title: Vegetation and rainfall departures side by side
recipes.question: Do vegetation departures and recent rainfall departures move in the same direction?
formula: V_ref(t) = monthly_departure area median for month t, for ref = all_years and ref = leave_one_year_out, each defined only where available
P(t) = catchment rainfall departure for month t from the 1991 to 2020 same-month mean, in mm
zero rule: values are compared as stored (V at four decimals, R_k at two); a month whose stored V_ref(t) or R_k(t) is 0 has no sign and is not counted
n_k(ref) = number of months with V_ref(t) and R_k(t) both defined and both non-zero
same_k(ref) = number of those months where V_ref(t) and R_k(t) have the same sign
all four windows and both references are reported together; none is selected

parameters.name: vegetation_departure_references
allowed: all_years
leave_one_year_out

parameters.name: zero_rule
allowed: stored V (four decimals) or R_k (two decimals) of 0: not counted
parameters.default: stored V (four decimals) or R_k (two decimals) of 0: not counted

parameters.name: stratum
allowed: catchment
parameters.default: catchment

sensitivitySet: windows 0, 1, 2 and 3 months and both vegetation references, always all eight counts

applicability.check: both series on the same geometry revision with shared period IDs

assumptions: Catchment-weighted CHIRPS cells represent the catchment's rainfall coarsely; vegetation can respond to rain within about 3 months
failureModes: Snow storage delays the response beyond 3 months; irrigated fields respond to water that is not rain; counts are not significance
standardLimitations: Counting months that move together shows co-occurrence; it does not estimate how much of a change rainfall explains.
Rainfall comes from 5 km grid cells, not from gauges in the valley.
A short record can hold months that move together by chance.
Values are compared as stored, V at four decimals and R_k at two; a month whose stored V or R_k is 0 has no sign and is left out of both counts.
Counts are given for both vegetation references side by side; with the all-years reference a 7-year median often equals the month's own value, so more months have V exactly 0.
recipes.registration: Catalog row before data; 1.0.0 formula written with the first run (all-years reference only, zero rule unstated). 1.1.0 is post hoc (2026-10-27, after the first results and an audit): it adds the leave-one-year-out reference side by side and states the zero rule; neither reference is preferred. 1.1.1 is post hoc too (2026-10-27, after a second audit): the zero rule applies to the stored values (V at four decimals, R_k at two), so the published rows reproduce the counts; this changes the all-years aligned counts from 46, 46, 46, 45 to 45, 45, 45, 44
recipes.postHocNote: Version 1.1.1 is post hoc: the leave-one-year-out reference and the zero rule were added after the first results (1.1.0), and the zero rule was applied to stored values after a second audit (1.1.1), all on 2026-10-27.
recipes.formulaPlain: Each month's vegetation departure is compared with rainfall departures summed over that month alone, and over windows reaching 1, 2 and 3 months back. Each window is counted separately. Months whose signs agree are counted, for both vegetation references.

recipes.title: Wet season against 1991 to 2020
recipes.question: Was a wet season's catchment rainfall below, near or above its 1991 to 2020 range?
formula: S(y) = sum of catchment rainfall totals from November of year y to April of year y + 1
reference: S(y) for the 30 wet seasons starting November 1991 to November 2020, sorted x(1) <= ... <= x(30)
category = below_normal if S < L; above_normal if S > U; otherwise near_normal
D = S - mean of the 30 reference totals, in mm

applicability.check: all 30 reference seasons and all six months of the season present

assumptions: The catchment-weighted CHIRPS total stands for the catchment's wet-season rainfall
failureModes: Statements about a larger area can differ from the catchment and still be true for their area; snowfall timing is invisible in a six-month total
standardLimitations: The category places this wet season among the 30 seasons of 1991 to 2020 for this catchment's CHIRPS grid cells; it is not a drought index and says nothing about cause.
Agreement compares directions only: a national statement can differ from one valley and still be correct for its own area.
CHIRPS cells are estimates for 5 km squares, not rain gauge readings.
recipes.registration: Full entry registered 2026-10-27 before any event comparison and without vegetation data
recipes.formulaPlain: The November to April catchment rainfall total is placed among the 30 wet seasons that start in 1991 to 2020. In the lowest third of that range it is below normal, in the highest third above normal, otherwise near normal.

recipes.title: Terrain sampling strata
recipes.question: Which parts of the catchment should field work sample separately?
recipes.registration: Written with the first run (2026-10-27); only a one-line strata bullet in data-sources-and-methods.md came before
formula: z = Copernicus DEM GLO-30 (2021) bilinear on a 30 m EPSG:32629 grid aligned with the 10 m analysis grid
elevation band: 1 if z < q(1/3), 2 if q(1/3) <= z < q(2/3), 3 if z >= q(2/3), q the quantiles of z over the catchment (equal-area terciles)
slope and aspect: Horn (1981) 3 x 3 gradient on the 30 m grid; aspect = downslope bearing from north
aspect class: level if slope < 5 deg; otherwise N (315 to 45 deg), E (45 to 135), S (135 to 225), W (225 to 315)
excluded: WorldCover 2021 class 40 (cropland) or 50 (built-up)
30 m classes repeated 3 x 3 onto the 10 m analysis grid

parameters.name: elevation_bands
allowed: equal-area terciles
parameters.default: equal-area terciles

parameters.name: aspect_classes
allowed: N E S W quadrants plus level
parameters.default: N E S W quadrants plus level

applicability.check: frozen catchment geometry and the pinned DEM release

assumptions: Elevation and aspect separate places that differ in snow, moisture and access, which field samples should cover
failureModes: Surface model raised by trees and buildings; radar artefacts in narrow gorges; WorldCover maps little cropland on the valley floor
standardLimitations: The DEM is a surface model: trees and buildings raise it; radar artefacts are possible in narrow gorges.
WorldCover 2021 is a 2021 context mask: it maps only 1.1% of the catchment as cropland, and much of the green valley floor is mapped as tree cover, which may include orchards.
Strata organize field sampling; they are not vegetation types, pasture units or management boundaries.
recipes.formulaPlain: The catchment is split into three equal-area elevation bands, and into north, east, south and west facing slopes plus level ground. WorldCover cropland and built-up areas are set aside.

recipes.title: Rainfall-adjusted greenness trend over the MODIS record
recipes.question: Once growing-season greenness is adjusted for the rain that came before it, does what is left drift up or down over about 25 seasons, for the catchment and for each terrain stratum?
recipes.registration: Full entry registered 2026-10-28 before any MODIS NDVI value was summarized or compared with rainfall. The raw MOD13Q1 windows were being downloaded while the entry was written; the download script prints item counts only. The windows, strata and thresholds come from the place configuration (science/places/<place>.json), fixed in the same way.
formula: NDVI(p, c) = DN / 10000 for Terra MOD13Q1 v6.1 composite c and 250 m pixel p, kept only where the composite's pixel reliability is 0 (good) or 1 (marginal) and -0.2 <= NDVI <= 1.0; reliability 2 (snow or ice), 3 (cloudy) and fill are not observed

Composites of season y and growing window W: the 16-day composite periods of the MODIS calendar (start days of year 1, 17, ..., 353) that start in a month of W in year y; a period with no Terra product in the archive read counts as a composite with nothing kept and is listed in the result
G(p, y, W) = mean of the kept NDVI(p, c) over the season's composites, defined only when at least half of the season's composite periods (rounded up) are kept at p
w_s(p) = number of 10 m analysis cells of stratum s whose centre falls in pixel p; the catchment is the stratum of all analysis cells
Y_s(y, W) = sum over p of w_s(p) G(p, y, W) / sum over p of w_s(p), over the pixels where G is defined; withheld when those pixels hold less than 70% of the stratum's weight

P_s(y, R) = rainfall total over rainfall window R ending in season y: for each month of R, the CHIRPS v3.0 monthly values of the 0.05 degree cells weighted by the number of 10 m analysis cells of stratum s whose centre falls in each cell, summed over the months
Rainfall fit: Y = a + b P by ordinary least squares over the n seasons with both values; b is reported with its 95% interval from the t distribution with n - 2 degrees of freedom, and R squared
e(y) = Y(y) - (a + b P(y)), the rainfall-adjusted residual of season y
Residual trend d = ordinary least squares slope of e on the season year (NDVI per year), with the 95% t interval (n - 2 degrees of freedom)

Autocorrelation-adjusted interval: the same slope with standard error scaled by sqrt((n - 2) / (n_eff - 2)), n_eff = n (1 - r1) / (1 + r1), r1 the lag-1 autocorrelation of the trend-fit residuals, n_eff = n when r1 <= 0, t quantile with n_eff - 2 degrees of freedom; withheld when n_eff < 3 (Santer et al. 2000)

Theil-Sen slope of e on the season year (median of pairwise slopes) with Sen's 95% interval from the ranks (N - C) / 2 and (N + C) / 2 + 1 of the N sorted pairwise slopes, C = 1.96 sqrt(n (n - 1) (2n + 5) / 18), no tie correction (Sen 1968)
Side by side: the ordinary least squares slope and 95% t interval of Y alone (unadjusted greenness) and of P alone (rainfall) on the season year

Precondition: when the 95% interval of b does not lie entirely above zero, the result for that stratum and window pair is labelled precondition_not_met; the residual trend is still stored but is not described as rainfall-adjusted
Direction wording: an interval entirely above zero is described as upward, entirely below zero as downward, otherwise as including zero (no direction stated)

parameters.name: growing_window
allowed: the growingWindows of the place configuration (Ait Bouguemez: mar_jun, mar_may, apr_jul)
parameters.default: the window marked primary (Ait Bouguemez: mar_jun)

parameters.name: rainfall_window
allowed: the rainfallWindows of the place configuration (Ait Bouguemez: sep_may, nov_apr)
parameters.default: the window marked primary (Ait Bouguemez: sep_may)

parameters.name: stratum
allowed: catchment
each class of each strata layer listed in the place configuration (Ait Bouguemez: three elevation bands, five aspect classes)
parameters.default: catchment

parameters.name: season_years
allowed: the seasonYears of the place configuration (Ait Bouguemez: 2000 to 2025)
parameters.default: the seasonYears of the place configuration

sensitivitySet: every growing window with every rainfall window, computed and stored together
pixel reliability 0 only (good) in place of 0 and 1
the autocorrelation-adjusted interval and the Theil-Sen slope with Sen's interval
the unadjusted greenness trend and the rainfall trend

applicability.check: seasons with both a greenness value and a rainfall value, for the stratum and window pair
applicability.minimum: 15 seasons; fewer and the pair is reported as insufficient_seasons with no slope

applicability.check: validated rainfall bundle covering every month of every rainfall window
frozen geometry and strata named in the place configuration, checksums matching

assumptions: In a dryland, growing-season greenness rises roughly in a straight line with the rain of the preceding months, so the residual removes most of the rainfall-driven year-to-year swing (Evans and Geerken 2004)
The relationship between greenness and rainfall is the same across the record; a change in that relationship shows up in the residual
failureModes: Weak or absent rainfall relationship (snowmelt or irrigation water, rainfall data error), flagged by the precondition
Mixed 250 m pixels on the valley floor where fields, orchards and slopes share a pixel
Persistent snow or cloud in spring removing upper-band composites
Terra orbit drift and sensor ageing changing NDVI in later seasons independently of vegetation
standardLimitations: The rainfall-adjusted residual still holds everything else that changes greenness: temperature, snow, irrigation, orchards and fields, grazing, fire, and sensor or orbit changes. It is not a measure of grazing impact or of degradation.

Trend methods can miss real change: in simulations for southern Africa, 30 to 40% degradation was needed before a trend showed under a rainfall-driven increase, and the residual method broke down at about 20% degradation (Wessels et al. 2012). An interval that includes zero is not evidence of no change.
Each 250 m MODIS pixel mixes surfaces; stratum values weight pixels by how much of the stratum falls inside them, so a mixed pixel counts toward more than one stratum.
Rainfall comes from 5 km CHIRPS grid cells, not from gauges in the valley, and snowfall is counted with rain.
Each stratum and window pair has its own interval. With many shown together, some intervals will exclude zero by chance alone.

Terra's overpass has drifted earlier since 2020, from 10:30 to about 9:06 mean local time by December 2025 (NASA): later seasons are seen with a lower sun and longer shadows in mountain terrain, which may shift NDVI without any change on the ground.
The windows were fixed before the MODIS values were read; other windows can give other slopes, which is why all registered windows are stored together.
recipes.formulaPlain: For each season since 2000, MODIS greenness from March to June is averaged over the catchment and each terrain stratum and set against the rain that fell from the previous September to May. A straight line through those pairs gives the greenness expected from the rain. What is left over each season is tested for an upward or downward drift across the years, with a 95% interval. The drift is a model estimate, and a drift does not by itself say why.

recipes.title: Monthly snow cover by elevation band
recipes.question: What share of each elevation band was snow-covered, month by month, from 2001 to 2025?
recipes.registration: Full entry registered 2026-10-28 before any MOD10A1 data was downloaded. The band sets come from the place configuration (science/places/<place>.json), fixed in the same way.
formula: v(p, d) = NDSI_Snow_Cover of Terra MOD10A1 v6.1 500 m pixel p on day d; clear when 0 <= v <= 100 (0 is snow-free land); cloud when v = 250; every other value (200 missing, 201 no decision, 211 night, 237 inland water, 239 ocean, 254 detector saturated, 255 fill) is not observed
snow_t(p, d) = 1 when p is clear on d and v >= 100 t, for the NDSI thresholds t = 0.2 (optimised for the Atlas, Bousbaa et al. 2024) and t = 0.4 (the global reference), computed side by side

w_b(p) = number of 10 m analysis cells of elevation band b whose centre falls in pixel p; elevation from the place's DEM, resampled to the analysis grid as for the terrain strata; band sets from the place configuration
clear_share(b, m) = sum over the days d of month m that have a product and over pixels p of w_b(p) clear(p, d) / sum over the same days and pixels of w_b(p)
snow_cover_fraction_t(b, m) = sum over d and p of w_b(p) snow_t(p, d) / sum over d and p of w_b(p) clear(p, d); reported only when clear_share(b, m) >= 0.3, otherwise insufficient_clear
product_days(m) = number of days of month m with a Terra MOD10A1 product over the place
The catchment as a whole is reported alongside the bands

parameters.name: band_set
allowed: the elevationBandSets of the place configuration (Ait Bouguemez: fixed_500m, terrain_strata)
parameters.default: the set marked primary (Ait Bouguemez: fixed_500m, edges 2000, 2500, 3000 and 3500 m)

parameters.name: months
allowed: the months of the place configuration (Ait Bouguemez: 2001-01 to 2025-12)
parameters.default: the months of the place configuration

sensitivitySet: NDSI threshold 0.2 and 0.4 side by side
fixed 500 m bands and the equal-area terrain strata bands side by side

applicability.check: elevation band with analysis cells inside the catchment
applicability.minimum: 1 analysis cell; a band with none is listed with no values

applicability.check: clear share of the band in the month
applicability.minimum: 0.3; below it the month is insufficient_clear

assumptions: On clear days, a 500 m pixel whose NDSI reaches the threshold is snow-covered as a whole
Clear days in a month are representative of the month's snow cover
failureModes: Persistent cloud during storms, leaving the snowiest days unobserved
Threshold bias in the Atlas: snow underestimated at NDSI 0.4
Shaded north-facing slopes and patchy or thin snow missed in a 500 m pixel
Terra orbit drift changing illumination in later years
standardLimitations: MOD10A1 sees snow only on clear days. Cloudy days are left out, not filled, so a month's fraction describes its clear days; the clear share is shown with it.

Against 448 Sentinel-2 scenes of the Atlas, Terra MODIS snow cover (version 6) was underestimated by 6.13% on average with the global NDSI threshold of 0.4 and overestimated by 0.34% with the Atlas threshold of 0.2 (Bousbaa et al. 2024). Both thresholds are shown.

Against five Atlas stations, MOD10A1 (version 5) agreed with snow observations 89% of the time (2000 to 2013, other Atlas catchments; Marchane et al. 2015). There is no station comparison for this valley.
Each 500 m pixel is called snow-covered or not as a whole; patchy snow, thin snow and snow on shaded slopes can be missed.
Snow cover is not snow depth or water: it says nothing about how much water the snow holds.

Terra's overpass has drifted earlier since 2020, from 10:30 to about 9:06 mean local time by December 2025 (NASA), so later years are seen with a lower sun and longer shadows, which may change snow detection on steep slopes.
recipes.formulaPlain: For every day from 2001 to 2025, MODIS marks each 500 m pixel as snow, snow-free or not seen (cloud, night, missing). For each elevation band and month, the snow-covered share is the snow pixel-days divided by the clear pixel-days. It is shown at two NDSI thresholds, 0.2 (fitted to the Atlas) and 0.4 (the global default), with the share of the band that was clear.

recipes.title: Where greenness rose or fell over the MODIS record, pixel by pixel
recipes.question: Across about 25 seasons, which 250 m pixels of the place grew greener or less green, how much of each elevation band and land cover group do they cover, and do any falling pixels form connected areas?
recipes.registration: Full entry registered 2026-10-28 before any per-pixel slope, any land-cover summary or any June to September greenness value was computed. When it was written the science lane had read the stratum results of restrend_long_record 1.0.0 (March to June, March to May and April to July; catchment, three elevation bands, five aspect classes): unadjusted greenness trends upward in every one of them, and greenness tracks antecedent rainfall weakly. Windows, area groups, cluster size and display scale come from the place configuration (science/places/<place>.json, revision 2).
formula: NDVI(p, c) = DN / 10000 for Terra MOD13Q1 v6.1 composite c and 250 m pixel p, kept only where the composite's pixel reliability is 0 (good) or 1 (marginal) and -0.2 <= NDVI <= 1.0, as in restrend_long_record

G(p, y, W) = mean of the kept NDVI(p, c) over the 16-day periods starting in a month of growing window W in year y, defined only when at least half of those periods (rounded up) are kept at p; a period with no Terra product on the archive read counts as nothing kept
Pixels: every MOD13Q1 pixel holding at least one 10 m analysis cell of the catchment; w(p) = number of those cells

Per pixel and window: over the season years where G is defined, the Theil-Sen slope of G on the year (median of pairwise slopes) with Sen's 95% interval from the ranks (N - C) / 2 and (N + C) / 2 + 1 of the N sorted pairwise slopes, C = 1.96 sqrt(n (n - 1) (2n + 5) / 18), no tie correction, as in restrend_long_record; fewer than 15 seasons and the pixel is insufficient_seasons

Per pixel: the Mann-Kendall statistic S with the tie-corrected variance n (n - 1) (2n + 5) / 18 minus the sum over tie groups of t (t - 1) (2t + 5) / 18, Z = (S - sign(S)) / sqrt(variance), two-sided p from the standard normal distribution
Pixel direction: Sen's interval entirely above zero is upward, entirely below zero downward, otherwise includes_zero

False discovery rate check: Benjamini-Hochberg at q = 0.05 over every pixel with a slope in the window; a pixel whose p passes keeps its direction as upward_fdr or downward_fdr when its Sen interval agrees, otherwise not_distinguished

Area groups: the catchment; each class of each strata layer listed in the configuration; the fixed elevation bands named in the configuration; the land cover groups of the configuration (WorldCover 2021 classes). For each group, the share of its 10 m analysis cells that lie in upward, downward, includes_zero and insufficient_seasons pixels, and the same for the false discovery rate classes. Under no change anywhere, about 2.5% of pixels per direction would show a per-pixel interval by chance; this is stated beside the shares

Connected areas: 8-connected groups of pixels sharing a false discovery rate direction (primary) or a per-pixel interval direction (sensitivity), of at least minClusterPixels pixels (Ait Bouguemez: 4, about 21 ha). For each: pixel count, catchment area in km2, centroid (longitude, latitude) weighted by catchment cells, median elevation of its catchment cells, land cover and aspect shares, median slope and its range. Every downward area is listed; upward areas are counted with the five largest listed

Display: for each window, the Theil-Sen slope in NDVI per decade averaged into the fixed EPSG:3857 grid of the map overviews (pixelM metres), painted with the light-theme data.ndvi-departure arms on the fixed domain of the configuration (Ait Bouguemez: -0.05 to +0.05 per decade, unpainted within 0.0025 of zero, t = (|d| - neutral) / (domain - neutral) clamped to 0..1, opacity 0.10 + 0.70 t, t in steps). No direction or false discovery rate class is drawn on the display

Data rasters: for each window, a GeoTIFF on the native MOD13Q1 grid with the slope, lower and upper bound per decade, and the number of seasons; no pixel-wise p-value or false discovery rate class is stored as a map raster (SCI-52)

per-pixel interval classes and false discovery rate classes side by side
connected areas from both class sets

applicability.check: seasons with a defined G at the pixel
applicability.minimum: 15; fewer and the pixel is insufficient_seasons

applicability.check: frozen geometry, strata and land cover named in the place configuration, checksums matching

assumptions: A straight-line drift over the season years describes the change at a pixel; a rise then fall can give a slope near zero
WorldCover 2021 describes each 10 m cell's land cover for the whole record
failureModes: With thousands of pixels, some intervals exclude zero by chance; reading single pixels overstates the evidence
Neighbouring pixels share weather, snow and sensor effects, so a connected area can come from one shared cause
Mixed 250 m pixels on the valley floor combine fields, orchards, villages and slopes
standardLimitations: Each pixel's interval is one of thousands. With no change anywhere, about 2.5% of pixels would still show an upward and 2.5% a downward interval at the 95% level, so the shares are shown beside a false discovery rate check (Benjamini and Hochberg 1995, q = 0.05), the control Wilks (2016) recommends when many locations are tested at once, and the map shows the slope only, not which pixels pass.

Neighbouring pixels are not independent: they share weather, snow and sensor effects. A connected area of pixels can arise from one shared cause, and the false discovery rate procedure was proved for independent tests.
Each 250 m MODIS pixel mixes surfaces. Land cover shares use ESA WorldCover 2021, a single 2021 map, applied to every season.

NDVI measures how green the ground looks from above, not forage, palatability or species: in Ait Bouguemez and the Central High Atlas, upper rangelands are dominated by spiny xerophytic vegetation over reduced short grasslands (SCI-19, p. 2), herders report the loss of palatable species (Astragalus armatus, Thymus satureioides) and the spread of unpalatable plants (Thymelaea virgata, Euphorbia nicaeensis) (SCI-03, pp. 7 to 8), and valley-floor apple orchards and irrigated fodder have expanded (SCI-03, pp. 5, 9 to 10; SCI-19, p. 9; SCI-105).

The June to September window spans the transition from late-spring pastoral agdal closure into open summer high-pasture grazing before transhumant flocks leave the valley in September and October (SCI-03, pp. 5 to 6, 12; SCI-19, pp. 2 to 5, Table 1; SCI-96); exact opening dates vary by village assembly and year.
These trends are not adjusted for rainfall; restrend_long_record states how closely the place's greenness follows antecedent rain.

Trend methods can miss real change: in simulations for southern Africa, 30 to 40% degradation was needed before a trend showed under a rainfall-driven increase (Wessels et al. 2012). An interval that includes zero is not evidence of no change.

In the spring windows, upper slopes are snow-covered for part of the window. Composites keep only pixels flagged good or marginal, but earlier or later snowmelt can change spring greenness with no change in the plants.

Terra's overpass has drifted earlier since 2020, from 10:30 to about 9:06 mean local time by December 2025 (NASA): later seasons are seen with a lower sun and longer shadows in mountain terrain, which may shift NDVI without any change on the ground.
recipes.formulaPlain: For each 250 m MODIS pixel, greenness is averaged over each season since 2000, and a robust straight-line slope through those seasons is computed with a 95% interval. The result says how much of each elevation band and land cover type lies in pixels that rose, fell or cannot be told apart from no change, checked against how many would rise or fall by chance among thousands of pixels. Falling pixels that touch each other are grouped and described. The map shows the slope only.

recipes.title: Greenness trends by season window, stratum and land cover over the MODIS record
recipes.question: Does the greenness trend differ between spring green-up and the June to September summer, for the catchment, its elevation bands, aspects and land cover groups?
recipes.registration: Full entry registered 2026-10-28 before any per-pixel slope, any land-cover summary or any June to September greenness value was computed. When it was written the science lane had read the stratum results of restrend_long_record 1.0.0 (March to June, March to May and April to July; catchment, three elevation bands, five aspect classes): unadjusted greenness trends upward in every one of them, and greenness tracks antecedent rainfall weakly. Windows, area groups, cluster size and display scale come from the place configuration (science/places/<place>.json, revision 2).
formula: NDVI(p, c) = DN / 10000 for Terra MOD13Q1 v6.1 composite c and 250 m pixel p, kept only where the composite's pixel reliability is 0 (good) or 1 (marginal) and -0.2 <= NDVI <= 1.0, as in restrend_long_record

G(p, y, W) = mean of the kept NDVI(p, c) over the 16-day periods starting in a month of growing window W in year y, defined only when at least half of those periods (rounded up) are kept at p; a period with no Terra product on the archive read counts as nothing kept

w_s(p) = number of 10 m analysis cells of stratum s whose centre falls in pixel p. Strata: the catchment, each class of each strata layer listed in the configuration, the fixed elevation bands named in the configuration and the land cover groups of the configuration
Y_s(y, W) = sum over p of w_s(p) G(p, y, W) / sum over p of w_s(p), over the pixels where G is defined; withheld when those pixels hold less than 70% of the stratum's weight (as restrend_long_record)

Trend: ordinary least squares slope of Y on the season year with the 95% t interval (n - 2 degrees of freedom) and its two-sided p; beside it the autocorrelation-adjusted interval (n_eff = n (1 - r1) / (1 + r1), Santer et al. 2000, withheld when n_eff < 3) and the Theil-Sen slope with Sen's 95% interval; fewer than 15 seasons and the pair is insufficient_seasons
False discovery rate check: Benjamini-Hochberg at q = 0.05 over every stratum and window pair with a slope, at pixel reliability 0 and 1; each pair states whether it passes. Every pair is reported

Season contrast: D_s(y) = Y_s(y, spring) - Y_s(y, summer) with the spring and summer windows of the configuration (Ait Bouguemez: mar_may and jun_sep); ordinary least squares slope of D on the year with the 95% t interval and the autocorrelation-adjusted interval, and the Theil-Sen slope. An interval entirely above zero means spring greenness rose faster (or fell slower) than summer greenness; entirely below zero, the reverse
Direction wording: an interval entirely above zero is upward, entirely below zero downward, otherwise includes zero (no direction stated)
Consistency: the catchment and terrain stratum values for the windows shared with restrend_long_record equal its stored season values

WorldCover 2021 describes each 10 m cell's land cover for the whole record

recipes.formulaPlain: Greenness is averaged over each season since 2000 for the catchment, its elevation bands, its aspects and its land cover types, in four windows: March to June, March to May, April to July and June to September. A straight line through the seasons gives a trend with a 95% interval. The spring (March to May) minus summer (June to September) difference is tested the same way, to see whether the two parts of the year changed differently.

recipes.title: Drainage network of the catchment
recipes.question: Along which channels does the catchment drain to its outlet, how much area drains to each segment, and how do the channels join?
recipes.registration: Full entry registered 2026-10-29, before this pipeline built any network. The 1.0 km2 threshold is the lead's brief; the conditioning is the catchment freeze's. The smoothing, simplification and spacing rules and the 30 m height surface were carried over from the 29 October specimen build of the valley model, which ran them first: the science lane had read that run's counts (233 segments, 20,785 vertices, none outside the frozen polygon) and how often the sampled surface rises along its lines (139 segments with some rise, 3 ending higher than they start). The 4.0 m rise tolerance comes from the DEM's stated relative vertical accuracy, not from that distribution. No hypothesis is tested: the recipe describes geometry. Place-specific values are in science/places/<place>.json, revision 3.
formula: Conditioning (a private step, as the catchment freeze geo_ait_bouguemez_catchment revision 1): Copernicus DEM GLO-30 (2021) on its native 1 arc-second EPSG:4326 grid, window 6.70 to 6.001 W and 31.40 to 31.85 N; pysheds 0.5 fill_pits, fill_depressions and resolve_flats; D8 flow direction with codes 64, 128, 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32 for north, north-east, east, south-east, south, south-west, west and north-west. Stored: the direction of each cell and the depression fill depth (fill_depressions(fill_pits(DEM)) minus DEM, m), cropped to the catchment's bounding box plus 8 cells
Outlet: the cell containing the frozen geometry's snapped outlet (31.6377778 N, 6.5372222 W)
Upstream area A(c) = sum of the WGS84 geodesic areas of the 1 x 1 arc-second cells whose D8 path passes through cell c, c included, in km2
Stream cells: catchment cells with A(c) >= 1.0 km2

Strahler order (Strahler 1957): a stream cell with no stream cell draining into it has order 1; where two or more of the stream cells draining into a cell share the highest incoming order m, the cell has order m + 1, otherwise m

Segments: a segment runs along the D8 path from a head (no stream cell upstream) or a confluence (two or more stream cells draining into it) to the next confluence or the outlet, both end cells included, so a segment ends where its downstream segment begins. Its order is the order of its first cell. Segments are numbered seg_001, seg_002 and so on by decreasing upstream area, ties by the row-major position of the first cell

Line: the segment's cell centres in EPSG:32629; one Chaikin corner-cutting pass keeping the end points; Douglas-Peucker simplification at 8 m; every straight piece divided into equal parts of at most 15 m; vertices converted to EPSG:4326 and stored to 7 decimals (about 1 cm)

Height: bilinear interpolation of the 30 m EPSG:32629 grid of the terrain strata recipe (Copernicus DEM GLO-30 bilinear to 30 m, aligned with the 10 m analysis grid, with 1 extra cell on every side, the grid the strata elevation bands are cut from), stored to 0.1 m as the third coordinate, metres above the EGM2008 geoid. The line is not forced downhill: where the surface rises along the path, the stored heights rise

Per segment: upstream area (the area draining through the segment's last cell before any confluence it ends at, km2 to 0.01) and the area at its first cell; the geodesic length of the stored line (m); net drop = first height minus last height; largest rise = the largest height of any vertex above the lowest vertex upstream of it; the largest fill depth over the D8 cells of the segment (m); the downstream segment and the upstream segments

Flag descends: true when the largest rise is at most 4.0 m and the net drop is positive, false otherwise. 4.0 m is the larger of the DEM's stated relative vertical accuracies (2 m on slopes up to 20%, 4 m above; SCI-168). Segments with descends false are listed with their largest fill depth; one whose largest fill depth is at least 4.0 m crosses a depression that filling raised by more than the tolerance

Sensitivity: stream cell count, number of heads and D8 path length (sum of geodesic distances between consecutive cell centres) at the thresholds 0.5, 1.0, 2.0 and 5.0 km2, stored together; only the 1.0 km2 network is drawn

Acceptance checks, all stored with the bundle: every vertex lies inside the frozen polygon (boundary included); the cells whose D8 path reaches the outlet equal the cells whose centres lie inside the frozen polygon; the outlet cell holds the largest accumulation among cells within 120 m of the freeze's input point; every stream cell drains to the outlet and no D8 path loops; the last vertex of the outlet segment is the snapped outlet and every other segment ends at its downstream segment's first vertex; the area at the outlet equals the polygon's geodesic area within 0.01 km2; the Strahler rule holds at every confluence of the segment graph; two runs give identical files apart from the computed time

parameters.name: height_surface
allowed: terrain_strata 30 m EPSG:32629 bilinear
parameters.default: terrain_strata 30 m EPSG:32629 bilinear

sensitivitySet: stream cells, heads and D8 path length at 0.5, 1.0, 2.0 and 5.0 km2 upstream area, stored together

applicability.check: frozen geometry and strata named in the place configuration, checksums matching
conditioned flow direction and fill depth rasters named in the place configuration, checksums matching

assumptions: Surface water leaves each cell towards the steepest-descending of its eight neighbours on the filled elevation surface
A drainage area of 1.0 km2 or more is a usable extent for drawing the valley's main channels; it is a drawing rule, not a channel head
failureModes: Irrigation canals, terraces, roads and bridges are not in the surface model and can send water elsewhere than the D8 path

Narrow gorges and closed hollows are poorly resolved at 30 m: depression filling routes flow across them and the line can rise along the surface, as in the lower gorge near the outlet where filling raised the surface by up to 58 m
standardLimitations: The network is drawn from a 30 m surface model, not mapped on the ground: trees, buildings, steep walls and radar artefacts distort the surface, and the D8 path can leave the real channel. No stream was checked in the field.

A segment is drawn wherever 1.0 km2 or more drains to a cell. The network's extent and length follow that threshold; it is not a measured channel head, and it does not separate streams that run all year from streams that run only after rain or snowmelt.

Depression filling and flat resolution route flow across closed hollows and the lower gorge, so some segments run where the 30 m surface rises along the line. Those segments are flagged, their heights are stored unchanged, and the line says nothing about how water moves there.

Upstream area counts the cells that drain to a point along D8 paths on the filled surface. It is not the share of rain that reaches the point, and it ignores irrigation canals, withdrawals and groundwater.
Strahler order counts how channels join. It says nothing about channel size, discharge or whether water is present.

Heights are metres above the EGM2008 geoid from the Copernicus DEM GLO-30 surface model, whose stated absolute vertical accuracy is under 4 m (90% linear error) and relative vertical accuracy under 2 m on slopes up to 20% and under 4 m above, as arithmetic means with local deviations possible (Copernicus DEM Product Handbook 5.0).
The catchment is a hydrological analysis extent, not a pasture, agdal or management boundary.
recipes.formulaPlain: Each cell of the 1 arc-second (about 30 m) Copernicus elevation model is given one downhill neighbour, after hollows are filled. The cells that 1 km2 or more of the catchment drains through are joined into segments from each head or junction to the next, numbered by how the channels join (Strahler order), and drawn as lines at the height of the surface.
